page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an L3 cache of 32 MB, vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as VAES and SHA-NI. The server comes bundled with 120 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one public IPv4 address without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong single-threaded instruction and compression throughput alongside throughput limitations typical of low core counts. Single-core execution achieves high ratings in stress-ng (3,610.59) as well as gzip compression (39.56 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.62 GB/sec). Large-block memory bandwidth registers balanced metrics at 45.94 GB/sec for uncached reads and 40.59 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, aggregate multi-core metrics, such as PassMark CPU (4,914.73) and multi-core Geekbench (2,259.0), place in the lower quartile across wider cloud benchmarks due to the physical constraint of having only a single dual-threaded execution core.

The hardware configuration provides reliable dedicated compute resources without the noise of shared virtual cores. While extensive parallel processing, large compilation jobs, and high-concurrency database queries show subdued performance in benchmarks, the instance remains cost-effective for tasks that rely on consistent per-thread capacity. It is primarily suited for lightweight web serving, API gateways, intermediate background worker queues, microservices, and small-scale caching layers like Redis.
description: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose cloud instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single multithreaded AMD EPYC physical core operating at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 8.0 GB of RAM alongside 120 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a complimentary public IPv4 address. Its x86_64 processor includes AVX-512 vector support, SHA-NI, and a 32 MB L3 cache. Benchmarks show high single-core performance, particularly in gzip compression and single-thread computational tests, alongside average uncached memory read and write speeds. However, aggregate multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-thread capacity, ranking lower in multi-threaded Geekbench, PassMark, and software compilation tests. Given its dedicated core allocation and balanced resource distribution, this configuration fits continuous lightweight workloads including static web serving, intermediate API layers, microservices, and entry-level transactional databases.
